hook: This tower took several rulers to finish.
takeaway: One tower. Several rulers. Eight centuries.

sources.title: Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi — UNESCO World Heritage Centre

shots.narration: This tower took several rulers to finish.
Qutb-ud-din Aibak began it around 1199, marking Delhi's new sultanate.
Only its first storey was finished under him.

visual.stillPrompt: Late twelfth century Delhi. The first storey of a tall red sandstone tower stands alone on a dusty plain, its surface freshly carved with deep fluting and bands of inscription. Wooden scaffolding leans against the stone. A few stonemasons in simple Sultanate-era robes work at ground level, seen from behind and at a distance. Low morning light rakes across the sandstone; dust hangs in the air.
visual.motionPrompt: a very slow push in toward the carved base of the tower

shots.narration: His successor Iltutmish added three more storeys above it.
The tower grew tall — sandstone below, marble and sandstone above.

visual.stillPrompt: Thirteenth century Delhi. A tall tapering minaret of five storeys rises above a walled mosque courtyard, the lower storeys in deep red sandstone with heavy fluting, the upper storeys in pale marble banded with sandstone. Small distant figures cross the courtyard below, giving scale. Late afternoon light, long shadows across worn stone paving.
visual.motionPrompt: a slow controlled tilt upward from the base of the tower to its top

shots.narration: Lightning damaged the top; Firoz Shah Tughlaq rebuilt it.

One tower. Several rulers. Eight centuries.
